newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian shares continue to surge.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian shares continue to surge.

text.p: Nigerian blue chips closed higher buoyed by strong demand, taking the all-share index to its fifth consecutive rise.
The index closed at 7085.78 from 7070.63 the previous day.
Most of Thursday's gains were in petroleum marketing and food shares, which traders said would remain buoyant whatever the direction of fiscal 1997 budget being anxiously awaited by the nation.
The biggest gainer in percentage terms was Industrial Gases, up 45 kobo to 12.00 naira after announcing a satisfactory 1996 result on Wednesday.
Cadbury moved fully onto the comeback trail, gaining 20 kobo at 21.80 naira.
Coca-Cola bottlers, Nigerian Bottling Company, rose 20 kobo to 31.31 naira, while Union Dicon Salt advanced 10 kobo to 43.35 naira.
Unipetrol was 50 kobo more at 62.50 naira, trailed by Total at 60.00 naira, up 25 kobo, and Mobil, 51 kobo stronger at 51.33 naira.
Packaging firm Carnaud Metal Box was down two kobo on the absence of buyers, closing at 2.81 naira.
Costain, the construction firm, traded five kobo down at 1.70 naira for the same reason, said traders.
